quest.title: Toys for the Children
quest.description: With Yelan's help, you locate Ashvapati's hideout. There lies a past buried beneath the yellow sands, and with it, the truth behind the entire case...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Part III
chapter.title: Toys for the Children

talks.objective: Wait until 07:00 – 10:00 two days from now
Go to the event venue to meet up with Yelan and the rest

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Took me a bit longer than I expected, but I've found where he's hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Let me just be sure of one thing... We're dealing with someone who has extremely dangerous weaponry in his hands. If it comes to it, are you prepared to handle the worst case scenario?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Absolutely. You just need to trust us, just like we trusted you earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Yeah, we've got this. My crew's already locked and loaded.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'll take you at your word.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I know you said you wanted to keep this operation small. But, I still thought you could use some backup.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, I chose a few promising young Spina members to help out. Clorinde and I have got things covered at the expo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we're ready to roll then.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Now that you're here, I guess we can get this show on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, you can't come with us. You need to stay at the expo like we agreed. It's for your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: We know. It's just... Do you really think Uncle Ashvapati is working for the bad guys?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I wish I could answer that question, but it would just be speculation, and I work based off evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: He's been gone for two days now, and he just left us here... He's never done that before. Maybe he really is working for those people and was afraid of getting caught...

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: But, if that's true, then... That means he must've been involved in making and selling weapons in the past, too. Wouldn't that make him a bad person...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's not for us to say. Take a look around the expo — there are plenty of other people making and selling weapons. Doesn't mean they're necessarily all bad people.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The same is true for your uncle. Whatever he may have done in the past, the real question we need to ask is "why." There's a lot we need to know before we can judge a person.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In Fontaine, we have a long and complicated process in place just to make sure we get the right answer to that question.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Yeah... Why would Uncle Ashvapati do something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How about this? I'll make sure that Miss Chevreuse and Miss Yelan promise to bring your uncle back safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then, you can ask him yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: Thanks, Miss!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: This situation is complicated and unpredictable. Isn't it a bit early to be making those kinds of promises?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, it's alright. We're prepared for whatever we might face.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Regardless, it's a promise we have to keep. After all, when the children get their answer, it will shape their understanding of what justice means.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Then let's all do our part to make sure this ends as well as it possibly can.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Stop right there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where is he?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: We missed him...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Looks like he left behind plenty of evidence, though. Search the area, let's see if we can find a lead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this what Paimon thinks it is?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's the display model that goes with the prototype... Guess that does make him our thief.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: What's worse is that, with his technical background, I bet he managed to bypass the security features on the prototype.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You're saying, our guy has a battle-ready ballista in his possession, just waiting to be unleashed?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't looking good...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Something isn't adding up... All the evidence suggests that he was here alone. Which begs the question: Why would he unlock the ballista's features before even meeting up with his boss?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That's a question for another time. We need to focus on where he's going next.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: These records look suspiciously familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Yeah... doesn't seem very coincidental to me, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Remember when I said this group's cover was ironclad? They were always careful never to leave a trail leading back to them...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The one time they slipped up, it broke the case wide open. We found a cargo manifest left behind at the scene — that's the clue that led us to Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: It was a similar story on our end.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And now, that same manifest shows up here, among the records left behind by Ashvapati.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... he's the guy that slipped up back then?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Unless it wasn't a slip-up at all... How does the same clue get left behind at two separate scenes, and picked up by two separate law-enforcement agencies? Thinking back on it now, it doesn't seem quite so accidental after all.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: No. Almost like he led us here on purpose... But, for what reason?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, there's a letter here.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Look at how it's positioned... it was begging to be found. I think it might be for us.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You think he knew we would come here?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: If he did, he's a more impressive opponent than I anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Let's keep going. We can read it together when we debrief.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Search the area. Let's see if we can find a lead.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Strange... Did he lead us here on purpose?

talks.objective: Summarize the information with Chevreuse and Yelan

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: This situation seems more complicated than we imagined. It looks like Ashvapati does have a connection to our criminal gang... But, it might not be what we thought at first.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You don't think he's working for them?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Unlikely. He lured us to Nod-Krai, prepared those weapons on his own, deliberately put us on his trail... This is looking more and more like the work of an independent actor.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Well, if we wanna get to the bottom of this, he's still our best lead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's read the letter.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That would seem to be our last remaining clue. Let's do it.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: To the officers of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol and the Liyue Qixing. You certainly live up to your reputation. Within a single day, you were able to eliminate over half of the gang's forces. I appreciate the effort.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I doubt my secret hiding spot will be a secret much longer, so I suppose it's my turn to throw my hat in the ring.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I'm just glad I no longer have to run. So, before my day in court is upon me, allow me to confess to my crimes.

talks.objective: Read the letter Ashvapati left behind

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: It all started with a Kshahrewar researcher, expelled from the Akademiya for violating a taboo.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: He had dedicated his life to the pursuit of knowledge, but when he found himself in the desert, it wasn't even worth a pail of water to quench his thirst.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: *coughing*... Could you spare some water? I... I'm a Kshahrewar researcher. If you need something, I could—

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Researchers like you are a dime a dozen. Smart as a whip until you find yourself in the desert... Then, you're lucky to survive the night.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Are... Are you mocking me?

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: No, son. Just still trying to figure out why I've got such a soft spot for strays like you... Here, give me your canteen.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: *gulp*...

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: You got somewhere to go?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: *coughing*... Not really. Thanks to this water, though, at least I can rule out the bottom of a vulture's stomach.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Haha... Now you're talking like desert folk. You could always join my band of misfits.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: What would I do?

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Gather foods, guard our water source... just like everyone else I've taken in.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Of course, if you have something you're good at, you're welcome to show it off. Every little bit helps.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: All I know is... weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Yeah! I love studying them! Big and powerful ones, small and deadly ones, old ones, new ones...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I believe the essence of Kshahrewar research is embodied in weaponry, and the pursuit of this kind of technology is what pushes the world forward.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: My lifelong goal has always been to become a foremost expert on all kinds of weapons so I can invent even more advanced ones!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: So, I might have "borrowed" a few sensitive texts without permission, but you see the vision, right? The higher-ups in the Akademiya just didn't understand...

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Pfft. The Akademiya could have a thousand and one reasons for exiling you out here, and it still wouldn't matter to me, son. All I care about is what this "specialty" of yours can do for us.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I... I can help upgrade your weaponry! That should come in handy in a dangerous place like the desert, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: True, weapons are essential to life here in the desert. Most folks get them when merchants happen to pass through.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: But when it comes to protecting the people here, this scimitar in my hand is more than enough. The kind of weapons you're talking about are overkill for a place like this.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Overkill? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Our group is lucky. Our ancestors learned how to protect the oasis from the sandstorms to prevent it from drying up.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Plus, we're pretty far off the beaten path. Helps us avoid conflict with other bands of Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: All in all, we don't have to travel to find water, we don't have to fight off other desert folk.... It's a real place to call home.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: There are plenty of ways to die in the desert, but behind a lot of them lies too much ambition. So, having somewhere to settle down... is more than enough for me.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I see... Guess I could do some odd jobs, then.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: I've heard you Kshahrewar scholars are handy with all kinds of gadgets. You could always make something for the kids...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: You mean like... toys?

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Yes, if you wouldn't mind. It'll give 'em something to do. Life can get boring out here.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Alright then...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: And just like that, a Kshahrewar scholar at the cutting edge of his field ended up in the desert... making toys for children.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: It got boring from time to time, but all in all, those days were quite pleasant. The Eremites accepted me as one of their own, and all the children loved me.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Looking back now, I wish I could have lived like that until the end of my days. But then those despicable people showed up, and it changed everything...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Don't rush me. These materials are in short supply.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Guard
dialogues.text: They've got a lot of nerve, showing their faces back here.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: Sennedjem... It has been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Well, we have a right to this oasis too. Our ancestors were part of the group that discovered it!

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Guard
dialogues.text: You hated this place! After that giant sandstorm, when everyone else was trying to figure out how to help, you got out of dodge the first chance you could get!

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Because I knew better than to be stubborn. Stay in one place too long around here, and it might just be your grave.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Guard
dialogues.text: You abandoned this place. If we'd done the same, the oasis wouldn't even exist anymore. You gave up your right to be here a long time ago!

dialogues.speaker: Eremite
dialogues.text: I heard they joined another band of Eremites after leaving us, but got kicked out. I bet they're only crawling back to us now because they've got nowhere else to go...

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Guard
dialogues.text: Chief, should we drive them off?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: I'd like to see you try! I'm warning you... You won't get rid of us that easily!

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: ...Leave them be. This oasis has always been big enough to sustain more than one group of people. It's not worth spilling blood over.

dialogues.speaker: Khaemwaset
dialogues.text: All that matters is keeping the people here safe.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: At the time, I didn't think much of it. Just Khaemwaset being the kind-hearted man he always had been.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: And so, normal life continued, much unchanged. Well, mostly. You can take the scholar out of the Akademiya, but... Putting your life's work behind you is easier said than done.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I often found myself flipping through my collection of blueprints and sketches. The Ruin Drakes scattered around Sumeru were of particular interest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: As far as I knew, no one had been able to analyze or reproduce the technology within those mechanisms.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: But I was able to design a kind of "lure" to bait them into attacking a specific target — in effect, turning them into a weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Somehow, the new arrivals at the oasis must've caught wind of it, because they soon started taking an interest in me.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Hope you don't mind me asking, but is that a weapon you're researching?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...I do mind, actually. It's none of your business.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Rumor is, you used to be a researcher at the Akademiya. All that knowledge going to waste out here in the sticks ... what a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: I want to team up.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: The rules and red tape that got you kicked out of the Akademiya... They don't exist in the desert. You could take this research to the next level. As things stand, all you've got is a blueprint and a pipe dream.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: But what if... you had access to the right funds and materials?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: What are you suggesting?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Me and my men can get you what you need. In return, all you gotta do is bring this sketch to life.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: We've always had a good eye for business, just never the right product. But this thing right here... the different bands of Eremites are gonna shell out Mora left and right to get their hands on it.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: You want to sell it?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: It's a win-win. You provide the goods, and I earn enough Mora from these people to fund the research of your dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I don't know...

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: I understand what you're worried about. But listen, it won't come back to bite the people here.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: These people don't think bigger than this place. They don't get involved in conflict. I mean, c'mon, their biggest enemy is the weather.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...You've made a bad name for yourself around here. I don't want any part in this.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Well, it's your choice. But it could be the last meaningful choice you ever get in life.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: So I'll ask you again. Do you want to finally develop the weapons you've been dreaming of, and realize your academic ambitions? Or do you want to stay here building toys for kids?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: How I wish I'd made the right choice back then...

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Yeah, we increased our prices. What about it? You gonna back out?

dialogues.speaker: Buyer
dialogues.text: So, you're really as money hungry as they all say, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Cash is king. That's just business.

dialogues.speaker: Buyer
dialogues.text: Hmph, fine.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...I'm done. I want out.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? We're making bank here.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I know what the weapons have been used for, and I refuse to be an accomplice to all this any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: An accomplice? Listen, that's got nothing to do with us. People would be at each other's throats with or without our weapons. So they die to a machine instead of a scimitar? What difference does it make?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Can't you sell more than just weapons? Surely this can't be all the Eremites are interested in buying?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: If you wanna make the big Mora, you gotta push what sells. That's just how it is.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: *sigh*... And that right there is why I want out.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Fine. I've made more than enough to leave this dump in the dust anyway. If you want out so bad, have it your way.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: What was that!?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Khaemwaset!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: How did this happen?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: You won't find a tribe in this desert without enemies. People have tried to steal water from this oasis in the past, but Khaemwaset drove them off. Guess his enemies have been holding a grudge this whole time...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: You sold weapons to his enemies? But, he took you in when you had nowhere to turn! You owe him your life! Why would you do this!?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: It was the perfect excuse to drive up the price, that's why.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: It was only later that I found out, this wasn't the first time Sennedjem and his men had turned around and stabbed their allies in the back. Let's just say... there was a good reason they had nowhere else to turn back then.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I didn't chase after them or try to hold them accountable. In that moment, all I could think about was saving as many people as I could in a desperate attempt to atone for my sins.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: But once the weapons I designed were turned against us, the fate of this place was sealed... even I could do nothing to prevent it.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: In the end, despite all the burning tents I rushed into, I was only able to save three children.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: And now you know the full account of my crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I've been raising them ever since, while attempting to hunt down the men who made them orphans in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: This confession is for the kids to read too, so I hope you'll pass it along to them. They deserve to know the full truth of what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I know I'm in no position to make requests, but... please help them find loving parents to take them in. Above all else, they deserve a true family.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Back then, I failed to see this through to the end. But I won't make that mistake again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez, if this is true...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: He's after the same target as us... and he's out for revenge.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He even lured us to Nod-Krai to help him get it.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I think I know what he's planning to do with those ballistas now. If I'm right, this doesn't bode well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then we need to find him ASAP! It sounds like he's about to do something super dangerous, but we promised the kids we'd bring him back safe.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I can't just let him get rid of our target either. This crime ring runs deep. There are still many other conspirators we need to track down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So where do we go to find him?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got something?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: He knew we'd be out of the picture investigating this place... I think he decided to spring the trap that we set up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's gonna ambush the target when he comes to pick up the goods...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, snap! He's not working for them, so our original plan could've worked all along!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The meeting will be happening any time now. Quick, we need to head to the rendezvous point.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Ashvapati?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Sennedjem. Over a decade at least...

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: How did you find this place?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: All these years, and the signal you use for the meet-up point still hasn't changed. All I had to do was pose as your point of contact, and fish a time and date out of that scout you sent.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Useless bunch of idiots... Just wait until my backup gets here.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Oh, I think that might take a while. The Fontaine and Liyue authorities have your men locked down tight... Every last one.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: No... There's no way the cops could have known we'd be here.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Unless, of course, someone deliberately left a trail of clues leading them straight to the expo. That would be a different story, now wouldn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: If they hadn't taken your agents out of the equation, I doubt I would've been able to lure you here.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Hmph, so now what? You gonna turn me in too?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: No. The authorities can have your men. But you're mine.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Is that Fatui tech? Looks like your skills are as good as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Listen, I know you're mad that I've been racking up Mora without you all these years. But it looks like you still got it. If you want back in, we can work something out.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: After everything that happened, what makes you think I would want back in?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Because what's the alternative? ...You're not here for revenge, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: After Khaemwaset took you in, you really convinced yourself you were one of them, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: What you should have learned is that banking on "loyalty" and "belonging" is a losing hand. Better to cash out before you're in the hole.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: In the desert, my people live by one rule and one rule alone — the last laugh doesn't go to the righteous... it belongs to the one who knows how to cut their losses.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Just look at me. When there's Mora to be earned in the desert, I'm a desert folk. When the opportunities in Fontaine are sweeter, I'm a Fontainian.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: You think everyone is as much of a lowlife as you?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: A lowlife? Heh, there's nothing Mora can't buy, Ashvapati... that includes prestige.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: You're talking to a renowned Fontainian philanthropist who lives in the Vasari Passage and spends his days going from one grand banquet to the next. Nobody who counts would dare call me a lowlife!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Are you done?

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: Tch... Clearly, there's no reasoning with you. Fine. Have it your way.

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: But if you want me dead so bad, why'd you come to face me alone? That wasn't the wisest decision, now, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Oh, don't you worry — I brought plenty of firepower with me. You could've brought a whole army for all I care. These weapons will bury every last one of you!

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: What the... Are you crazy!? If that thing fires, you're not getting out of here alive either!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Yes, that's the plan. It's high time both of us paid the price for our sins!

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: He's lost his mind... Get him! Start breaking his bones until he removes this barrier!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hold it right there, all of you! Otherwise, I've got enough firepower to go around too!

dialogues.speaker: Sennedjem
dialogues.text: The Maison Gardiennage...

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: You got here sooner than I expected...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's that in the sky? Looks like bad news...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Ashvapati, you have my word that these people will face the judgment of the Fontaine courts. Remove the barrier and come with us at once!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Fontainian justice is too merciful for them... You should leave us.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Stubborn fool...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ati, Neb, and Raya are waiting for you!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I don't deserve them... I have to atone for the things I've done.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: What is it you feel you need to atone for? Weapons research?

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...You're from Liyue, right? Your ancestors were the first people to master the recipe for gunpowder. And yet, they turned it into fireworks and firecrackers that even children could play with.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: Surely, it's choices like that which make Liyue what it is today... I hear that it's a very peaceful place to live for the most part.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: But me? I chose to use my research skills to create weapons of war that brought death to countless people and destroyed the only home those kids had... That's why I have to atone. Because I have blood on my hands.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Sounds like you don't know as much as you think about fireworks. They might be harmless fun in this day and age, but they started out as weapons too, y'know.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: That's right. Fireworks and firecrackers were originally developed for use as weapons. They needed something a little more powerful than usual for purging evil forces and scaring off wild beasts.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Over time, evil spirits learned to fear the sight of flames, and the beasts retreated into the mountains. That's when people started repurposing fireworks for entertainment purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: The peace we enjoy today isn't because we chose to make toys instead of weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: The weapons are what secured us the peace in the first place. Only then did we have the luxury of choosing to turn them into toys instead.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: It's people, not weapons, that commit acts of evil. And when people are as bent on destruction as the evil forces and beasts faced by our forebears, whatever tools they have at their disposal end up as weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: ...Time is running out. Please, leave while you still can.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Relax. Now that we have these guys in custody, I think we can find a way of repurposing these ballistas for the children's amusement.

dialogues.speaker: Special Security and Surveillance Patrol Member
dialogues.text: No funny business!

dialogues.speaker: Ashvapati
dialogues.text: I never imagined the Guizhong Ballista could be used for something so beautiful...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: If you'll agree to come with us and answer some questions, it would be a big help to our investigation.

response.speaker: Ashvapati
response.text: Of course. You'll have my full cooperation. I know I'm guilty, just... not sure of the precise crime at this point.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Honestly, me neither. I'm sure a case like yours would have Fontaine's top legal experts scratching their heads.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: As for these arms dealers, though... I can confidently say that none of them will be getting away with this. So at least you can take some solace in that.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I know, there's no sentence the court can give them that will satisfy you. But at least the trial will be a public declaration of their crimes and the punishment they will receive. The victims deserve that much.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Considering the alternative was them dying in obscurity to a revenge-killing, with no one left behind to tell the story... This looks more like real justice to me.

choices.text: I didn't see this coming, either.
